declared_framework.machine_checkable_note: This sub-block is the part of the declaration the engine can confront with the computation. It SELECTS the basis generator -- concomitant_generator = linear_strain_tensor routes to the elasticity generator, riemann_tensor routes to the curvature generator -- and every field is then re-measured off the arrays that generator actually built. Any disagreement raises FrameworkMismatch and no receipt is sealed. The free-text keys below are prose for a reader and are never trusted. tensor_symmetry refers to the Cauchy stress the law produces, which is measured on the bank; the minor and major symmetries of the elasticity tensor itself are declared as CONSTRAINTS below, because whether they bind is a thing the search is supposed to find out.
declared_framework.geometry: flat Euclidean d-space in Cartesian coordinates: the metric is the constant Kronecker delta, the connection and the Riemann tensor of that metric are computed and come out identically zero, and partial derivatives are covariant derivatives
declared_framework.tensor_symmetry: the elasticity tensor C_ijkl; its minor and major symmetries are declared as constraints, not as part of the framework
declared_framework.concomitant_class: linear in the linear strain tensor eps_ij = (d_i u_j + d_j u_i)/2, with constant coefficients built from the Kronecker delta alone
declared_framework.conservation_motivation: angular momentum balance forces the Cauchy stress to be symmetric; the existence of a strain-energy function forces the major symmetry of C
declared_framework.provenance: EVERY item in this block was DECLARED by the operator. None of it was discovered by the search. The search derives only what these declarations force.
not_declared_and_therefore_derived: how many independent rank-4 tensors flat isotropic space offers
how far the declared symmetries collapse that count
that the surviving space in d >= 2 is exactly two-dimensional
that it is spanned by d_ij d_kl and d_ik d_jl + d_il d_jk, the Lame constants
that the minor symmetry of C did not need declaring because a symmetric Cauchy stress already forces it
that d_ik d_jl - d_il d_jk is a non-zero rank-4 tensor that is invisible to elasticity
the coefficients of the static equilibrium operator those constants force
that d = 1 collapses to a single elastic constant

arithmetic.sample_count_rationale: The rank-4 pattern space has three members and the collapse is measured by their action on the strain of each displacement jet, which contributes d*d*(jet size) independent constraints per sample -- far more than the three needed to separate three patterns. Five samples is therefore already generous, and the sampling error is one-sided in any case: too few samples can only report the admissible space too LARGE. The equilibrium fit needs the two operator rows to be independent, which one generic jet already delivers for d >= 2.

searches.purpose: the headline: what flat isotropic three-space, a rank-4 law linear in the strain, and a symmetric stress force
deliberately wrong constraint set: let the law contract the raw displacement gradient and drop the stress symmetry, and the space must grow
declare only that the Cauchy stress is symmetric, keep the raw gradient as the argument, and find out whether the minor symmetry had to be declared at all
the historically wrong rari-constant hypothesis lambda = mu; the space must shrink to a single constant
two dimensions: the same two constants, confirming the count is not a three-space accident
